title: Farro and Roasted Vegetable Bowl
subtitle: Nutty farro with squash, chickpeas, kale, and tahini dressing
excerpt: Chewy farro topped with roasted butternut squash, crispy chickpeas, wilted kale, and a lemony tahini dressing. A filling bowl that works for lunch or dinner.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from contemporary grain bowl recipes. Roasting chickpeas alongside the squash saves time and adds texture.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the farro up to 2 days ahead. Store in the fridge and reheat with a splash of water.

content.text: Pat the chickpeas dry before roasting. Any moisture will prevent them from going crisp.

items.prepNote: tough stems removed, leaves roughly torn

content.text: Heat the oven to 200C. Toss the squash and chickpeas in 3 tablespoons of olive oil. Season well. Spread over a large roasting tin in a single layer.
Roast for 30 to 35 minutes. Shake the tin halfway through. The chickpeas should be crispy and the squash tender.
Meanwhile, cook the farro in a large saucepan of salted boiling water for 25 to 30 minutes until chewy and tender. Drain well.
Make the dressing. Whisk together the tahini, lemon juice, cumin, honey, and 3 tablespoons of water until smooth. Season with salt.
Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Add the kale and toss for 2 minutes until wilted. Season.
Divide the farro between four bowls. Top with squash, chickpeas, and wilted kale. Drizzle the tahini dressing over everything.

items.symptom: Chickpeas are soft and chewy, not crispy.
items.fix: Spread on a dry tea towel and press firmly before oiling.
Add water one tablespoon at a time until it pours easily.

items.symptom: Farro is still chewy after 30 minutes.
items.cause: Farro was not soaked and needs longer cooking.
items.fix: Keep simmering and taste every 5 minutes until tender.
